form.create: Create a form and its empty first draft in a workspace this user may create in. The id is minted from the slug and never changes. The form's title is authored in the builder afterwards; creating it changes nothing a respondent can reach.
apply-draft: Apply the draft you proposed with propose_draft to this form's working draft, for the user to review as a diff and confirm. Call propose_draft first. It publishes nothing and releases nothing: the draft is stored as a draft and marked agent-assisted.
form.saveDraft: Save a complete draft to a form, through the same save path every edit in the builder takes. It publishes nothing and releases nothing: the draft is stored as a draft and marked agent-assisted. This is how a form goes from blank to a reviewable draft, after form.create and any question.create steps of the same plan.
form.publish: Publish the form's working draft to one environment: freeze it as the next version and make that version live there, in one act. Needs Edit forms and Publish forms for that environment. Where a non-prod environment exists a draft is never published straight to prod. The workflow and second approval apply exactly as they do on the screen.
form.release: Publish an existing version to one environment, including an earlier one (rollback). Nothing is frozen. Prod accepts only a version already live in a non-prod environment, where one exists. The workflow revision, the destination's release state and second approval are all rechecked at confirmation, so a stale review is refused and writes nothing, exactly as on the screen.
form.settings: Change the form's abuse-control settings. It affects sessions started from now on and leaves every session already under way untouched.
form.close: Close the form to new sessions in the current environment. Every session already under way keeps its pinned version and finishes normally.
form.reopen: Reopen the form to new sessions in the current environment.
link.mint: Mint one-time or reusable respondent links in the current environment. The URLs are shown to the user once and are never returned to you.
link.revoke: Revoke one respondent link in the current environment.
response.erase: Erase one respondent's answers and submission, recording a tombstone. It cannot be undone, and the user retypes the session id on the card before it can run.
response.unflag: Release one flagged response's withheld submission event, so its consumers receive it.
response.export: Open the export dialog with these filters. The user presses Export and the file downloads in their browser; no part of it is returned to you.
webhook.create: Configure a new delivery endpoint for this form in the current environment. Its signing secret is shown to the user once and is never returned to you.
webhook.rotate: Replace an endpoint's signing secret. Deliveries signed with the old one stop verifying, and the new secret is shown to the user once.
webhook.retarget: Point an endpoint at another URL. The card names the endpoint and shows the new target in full, query string included.
webhook.reactivate: Put a deactivated endpoint back in service in the current environment.
webhook.deactivate: Stop delivering to an endpoint. The row and its delivery history stay, and a delivery already in flight keeps its own retry state.
webhook.redeliver: Reset one dead-lettered delivery to due-now, so the worker attempts it again. It reads no part of the payload.
access.groupCreate: Create an access group in a workspace. The group grants nobody anything until somebody holds it, so creating one changes no access by itself.
access.groupRemove: Remove an access group and every grant it carried. Each holder loses that access at once, and one revoke row is written for each.
access.grant: Grant an access group to one person, by address. A self-grant of a response role is refused while the workspace requires a second approver.
access.revoke: Revoke one person's hold on an access group. Every other holder keeps theirs.
member.role: Make a member an owner of the workspace, or take ownership away. Removing the last owner is refused.
workspace.settings: Change the workspace's second-approver switch: whether a production release and a response self-grant need a second account.
question.create: Create a question and its draft v1 in the library. The id is minted once and never changes. Nothing pins the question until a form's draft does, and nothing serves it until the version is published.
question.saveDraft: Replace a draft version's definition. A published or deprecated version is refused: published content is immutable, so changing one means opening a new version.
question.publish: Freeze a draft version and make it pinnable. Its content can never change again, and a form's draft that pins it stops reporting an unpublished pin.
question.deprecate: Block new pins on a published version. Every form already pinned to it is untouched and keeps serving it.
question.newVersion: Open a new draft version, seeded from the latest one. Nothing published changes, and no form moves to it until a draft pins the new version.
